patch.title: Lyra Storage: 500 MW Battery Queue Project in Borden County, Texas
patch.description: ERCOT lists Lyra Storage, queue 26INR0636, as a 500 MW Borden County project. Its published planning target is November 12, 2026; current delivery, owner and cost need further verification.

references.title: EIR Oncor and AEPSC Drill Hole to Sand Lake to Solstice 765-kV Line Project Status Update — RPG October 2025

patch.longFormSummary:
• ERCOT’s planning appendix identifies Lyra Storage as queue 26INR0636: 500 MW in Borden County, Texas.
  • Timeline: the October 2025 planning presentation gives a projected COD of November 12, 2026. This is a planning target, not evidence of energization.
  • The cited ERCOT record does not establish the owner, project cost or storage duration; previous unsupported financing and duration claims have been removed.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: ERCOT October 2025 planning appendix, page 12: projected COD 11/12/2026 for 26INR0636. Estimated historical queue target; current delivery needs confirmation.

gaps: PUCT Lyra BESS SGIA 35077_2225_1531568.PDF found but blocked by plain curl (403); SB Energy subsidiary list alone does not establish this queue project’s ownership. Verify current queue, owner, duration, exact parcel and COD.

power.note: ERCOT planning queue 26INR0636; proposed maximum capacity, not operational capacity.

patch.title: Ameresco–CyrusOne NAS Lemoore: Proposed 100 MW AI Data Center and Energy Infrastructure
patch.description: Ameresco, CyrusOne and the U.S. Navy plan a 100 MW AI data center at NAS Lemoore, with onsite generation and a naval-base microgrid. First delivery is expected in 2027; the operator page does not publish a project cost.

references.title: NAS Lemoore Data Center Energy Project

patch.longFormSummary:
• The proposed 100 MW AI data center is a partnership involving Ameresco, CyrusOne and the U.S. Navy at NAS Lemoore, California.
  • Dedicated onsite generation would support the data center; the naval installation would receive a microgrid, engine generators, controls and infrastructure upgrades.
  • Timeline: Ameresco expects the first portion online in 2027 on land leased from the Department of Defense. The page says development agreements are being finalized.
  • A total investment is not published on this page; the earlier $1 billion amount is removed.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Ameresco states first portion expected online in 2027. January 1 is a year-only placeholder, not a promised day.

gaps: Exact parcel and current contracting/construction status require confirmation.

power.note: Proposed AI data center capacity per Ameresco.

patch.title: Applied Digital Adair County Data Center Proposal: Current Delivery Unverified
patch.description: Adair County’s April 2024 minutes document discussion of Applied Digital’s data center proposal. The opening date, current project scope and investment remain unverified; September 2026 reporting says no developer had approached the county with current plans.

references.title: Adair County Board of Supervisors — April 24, 2024 minutes
Adair County Supervisors Hold Public Hearing on Data Center Ordinance

patch.longFormSummary:
• County minutes record discussion of Applied Digital’s proposed data center during the April 24, 2024 setback-ordinance hearing.
  • Supervisors debated effects on neighbors and farmland. These minutes support a proposal, not a construction start or operating facility.
  • September 23, 2026 local reporting says supervisors had received no current developer plans for a county data center.
  • Timeline: the previous September 2027 tracker date is retained only as an unverified estimated placeholder pending current developer or county evidence. The claimed $1.5 billion cost and 200 MW capacity are not established by these opened records.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Unverified legacy tracker placeholder: September 2027. Opened April 2024 county minutes establish a proposal but no COD; September 2026 reporting raises current-status uncertainty. Do not treat as a confirmed opening.

gaps: Current status conflicts with legacy proposal: obtain developer response and October 14, 2026 ordinance outcome; confirm capacity, COD and parcel. Existing map/media are not newly site-verified.

patch.title: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1: 250 MW Operating, 400 MW Contracted IT Capacity
patch.description: Applied Digital reported 250 MW of operational critical IT capacity at Polaris Forge 1 in Ellendale on October 2, 2026. The full contracted deployment is 400 MW; the first 50 MW phase reached service on October 27, 2025.

references.title: Applied Digital Brings an Additional 75 MW of AI Infrastructure Online at Polaris Forge 1
Applied Digital Achieves Ready for Service for Phase 1 at Polaris Forge 1 Building 1 for CoreWeave

patch.longFormSummary:
• On October 2, 2026, Applied Digital completed the second 75 MW phase of Building 2, bringing the campus to 250 MW of operational critical IT load.
  • The fully leased campus is contracted for 400 MW at full buildout; operational load and planned buildout are different measures.
  • Timeline: the first 50 MW phase reached service on October 27, 2025. Later buildings have separate delivery dates; March 2026 was not the campus’s initial service date.
  • The earlier release identifies CoreWeave as the tenant. Its approximately $11 billion anticipated lease revenue is not a construction cost.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Applied Digital October 27, 2025 release confirms first 50 MW phase Ready for Service on that date; campus delivery is phased. October 2, 2026 release confirms 250 MW then operating.

gaps: Full 400 MW completion date and current campus capital cost remain unverified.

power.note: Operational critical IT capacity on October 2, 2026; 400 MW contracted buildout is not current operation.

patch.title: AVAIO Taurus: $6 Billion Campus, Initial 116 MW Phase in Brandon, Mississippi
patch.description: AVAIO’s Taurus campus in Brandon has a published $6 billion investment and initial 116 MW phase. Its current project listing gives Q3 2027 energization, later than the first-half 2027 target in its September 2025 announcement.

references.title: AVAIO Digital Breaks Ground on $6 Billion Brandon Data Center Campus; Leading Mississippi Contractor Begins Site Work

patch.longFormSummary:
• AVAIO’s September 10, 2025 announcement records site work beginning on a $6 billion, 329-acre Taurus campus with Yates Construction.
  • The first phase comprises over 600,000 square feet and 116 MW. An electric-service agreement with Entergy was executed in August 2025.
  • Timeline: the announcement targeted first-half 2027 delivery; the current operator listing gives Q3 2027 energization. July 1 represents the start of that quarter, not a scheduled day.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Checked October 23, 2026: current AVAIO project listing gives 116 MW energized Q3 2027, superseding older H1 2027 announcement. July 1 is quarter-only placeholder.

gaps: Exact site coordinates and phased full-campus delivery still require parcel-level verification.

patch.title: Cloverleaf Project Bluestem: Kansas Data Center Rezoning Active; Power-Plant Application Withdrawn
patch.description: Cloverleaf said on September 28, 2026 that its Project Bluestem data center rezoning remained active while it withdrew the initial application for a separate power-generation facility. Final capacity, investment and delivery date require verification.

references.title: Cloverleaf Evaluating Alternative Locations for Power Generation Facility

patch.longFormSummary:
• Cloverleaf withdrew its initial generation-facility application on September 28, 2026 while evaluating other sites. Its data center rezoning application remained active.
  • The project is near Tonganoxie Business Park in Leavenworth County. The FAQ says Evergy is studying available capacity and describes grid supply.
  • The FAQ’s statement that no formal applications had been submitted is older than the September 2026 update and should not be read as current status.
  • Timeline: no COD is stated in these opened operator records. The legacy December 2028 date remains only an unverified estimated tracker placeholder; no fixed capacity or cost is asserted here.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: December 2028 is an unverified legacy tracker placeholder, not a COD confirmed by Cloverleaf. September 28, 2026 update supports active data center rezoning only.

gaps: Obtain current county rezoning filing, final capacity, COD, tenant and exact site; 600–1,200 MW range is not established by these operator records.

patch.title: Crane Forest Grove Campus: 100+ MW Plan; $275.26M Qualified-Property Investment
patch.description: Crane advertises a 100+ MW Forest Grove campus near Hillsboro. A June 2025 city enterprise-zone contract records $275,259,195 of estimated qualified-property investment; this is a disclosed investment scope, not a verified all-in campus cost.

references.title: Data Centers: Oregon — Crane Data Centers
City of Forest Grove Enterprise Zone Property Tax Abatement Contract No. 25-001

patch.longFormSummary:
• Crane’s campus page advertises 100+ MW capacity. PDX01 has two 24 MW phases; PDX02 is approximately 48 MW.
  • The June 2025 Forest Grove contract identifies estimated qualified-property investment of $275,259,195 and tax lot 153050001300. This figure is not presented as an all-in campus construction budget.
  • Timeline: the operator page advertises Q3 2026 ready for service, which has passed. No commissioning announcement was verified; the existing December 31, 2026 date remains an unverified placeholder rather than an operator-stated revised COD.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Operator advertises Q3 2026 ready for service, now past; actual commissioning or revised COD not verified. Existing December 31, 2026 is a legacy estimated placeholder, not a revised operator target.

gaps: Obtain commissioning or revised schedule, confirm coordinate against filed parcel and distinguish qualified investment from total campus budget.

power.note: Operator advertises 100+ MW campus capacity; 100 is a lower bound, not measured operating demand.

patch.title: Metrobloks Southfield DTW-D: 89 MW Critical IT Plan; Investment Estimates Conflict
patch.description: Metrobloks currently advertises 89 MW of critical IT capacity for DTW-D at 27500 Inkster Road, Southfield. Earlier approval reporting described 100 MW total power and conflicting $500 million and $1.5 billion investment estimates.
patch.longFormSummary:
• Metrobloks lists DTW-D at 27500 Inkster Road with 89 MW critical IT capacity, one building with two floors and DTE/ITC power infrastructure.
  • Approval reporting describes 100 MW power demand. Critical IT load and facility power differ; the two numbers should not be treated as equivalent.
  • Planet Detroit reports a $1.5 billion two-phase estimate and $500 million in the presentation deck, explicitly noting the discrepancy. The single numeric price is cleared pending reconciliation.
  • Timeline: the operator page says coming soon without an opening date. June 2027 remains an unverified legacy estimated placeholder.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: Operator says coming soon without a COD. June 2027 is an unverified legacy tracker placeholder; requires developer confirmation.

gaps: Resolve $500M/$1.5B scope discrepancy, current COD and differing acreage/floor-area figures; map coordinates not newly parcel-verified.

power.note: Advertised critical IT capacity; prior 100 MW reporting concerns facility power, not the same metric.

patch.title: Microsoft San Jose Data Center: Up to 99 MW at 1657 Alviso-Milpitas Road
patch.description: The California Energy Commission identifies Microsoft’s two-building San Jose project at 1657 Alviso-Milpitas Road, with a maximum electrical load of 99 MW and estimated load of 77 MW. A verified total project budget and COD remain unavailable.

references.title: San Jose Data Center — California Energy Commission

patch.longFormSummary:
• CEC docket 19-SPPE-04 identifies Microsoft as owner of the two-building project at 1657 Alviso-Milpitas Road.
  • The CEC describes up to 99 MW maximum electrical load, with an estimated 77 MW inclusive of IT, ancillary equipment and other facility loads.
  • The published design includes an onsite 115 kV substation supplied from PG&E’s adjacent Los Esteros Substation.
  • The CEC lists a Small Power Plant Exemption, which is not proof of operational status. The earlier $73.2 million land figure is removed from the total-project price field.
  • Timeline: no COD is published on this CEC page. June 2028 remains only an unverified legacy estimated tracker placeholder.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: June 2028 is an unverified legacy tracker placeholder. CEC project page provides permitting and design information but no COD.

gaps: Verify current city addendum, generator design, construction/COD, full project cost and coordinates; prior land acquisition cost was not a campus construction cost.

power.note: CEC design maximum load, not operating demand; CEC estimates 77 MW facility load.

patch.title: QTS Cedar Rapids: Planned $10 Billion, Seven-Building Data Center Campus
patch.description: QTS’s August 8, 2025 announcement describes a planned $10 billion campus with seven data center buildings on 612 acres in Big Cedar Industrial Center. The announcement does not publish power capacity or a service date.

references.title: QTS Announces New, World-Class Data Center Campus in Cedar Rapids

patch.longFormSummary:
• QTS announced a planned $10 billion investment in Cedar Rapids on August 8, 2025, comprising seven data center buildings across 612 acres.
  • QTS identifies Alliant Energy as its utility partner and describes water-free cooling for the campus.
  • The announcement does not substantiate the earlier 1,100 MW figure, so it is removed rather than presented as a confirmed specification.
  • Timeline: no commercial-operation date is stated in this release. December 2027 remains an unverified legacy estimated tracker placeholder, pending a current utility or operator schedule.
patch.dateConfidenceReasoning: December 2027 is an unverified legacy tracker placeholder. QTS August 8, 2025 announcement establishes investment and scope but does not state COD.

gaps: Resolve reported power-capacity differences using current utility contract/filings; confirm phased COD, current construction status and parcel coordinates.
